depth_history.shortcut_targeted: The binary state set makes s_u × s_v = 2 equivalent to requiring every critical-pair edge to connect opposite colors, so the whole task is ordinary graph bipartiteness plus component orientation.
depth_history.edit_summary: Replace the uniform condition s_u × s_v = 2 with a pair-dependent equilibrium condition: if n is even, require product 2; if n is odd, require product 1 for every pair incident to sensor 1 and product 2 for every other pair. Keep the input and output formats unchanged. The provided even-n example remains valid, while the odd-n triangle remains impossible but ordinary bipartite-coloring solutions no longer solve all cases.

depth_history.edit_summary: No safe edit preserves the stated task while defeating these solutions. If changing the task is permitted, add a global requirement such as requiring exactly floor(n/2) sensors to use mode 1; the existing bipartite-coloring solutions do not check that condition.

depth_history.shortcut_targeted: The immutable two-value amplitude domain combined with the exactly-twice edge constraint is equivalent to requiring a proper 2-coloring of the input graph.
depth_history.edit_summary: No edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the stated task: bipartite coloring is the intrinsic mathematical structure. Any effective edit would have to change the core constraint or the allowed-value domain, which would also change the problem.
